_comment: LoopStar Style-picker registry (LP.6 MG.1b). Lists the generative material packs a user can pick as a genre FEEL for 'Make it new', independent of the loaded sound pack. Each id has a sibling {id}/material.json. Read by LoopStarGenreStore.availableStyles(). RULE #1: content, zero-rebuild.

styles.name: Soul
styles.blurb: Motown / Stax soul: a ghost-note backbeat pocket, rootless Rhodes 7th/9th voicings, and a melodic finger bass.

styles.name: Funk
styles.blurb: Classic funk: ghost-note 16th pocket, staccato rootless-9th chank comping, and a greasy root-octave bass that lives on the One.

styles.name: Boom-Bap
styles.blurb: 90s boom-bap: a dusty MPC-swung kick+snare, a rootless Rhodes sample-flip chopped into stabs, a pedal sub, and a lonesome sax line.

styles.name: Trap
styles.blurb: Modern trap: a booming TR-808 sub that glides under a dark minor loop, straight machine-gun hats, and a spacious bell hook.

styles.name: House
styles.blurb: Classic / deep house: a four-on-the-floor pulse, hissing offbeat open hats, and pumping rootless Rhodes stabs over a warm synth-bass bounce.

styles.name: Dubstep
styles.blurb: Half-time menace at 140 that breathes like 70 — cavernous sub, iron snare, and a whole lot of dark air.

styles.name: Drum & Bass
styles.blurb: Liquid jungle at 174: a chopped breakbeat sprints while a rolling reese sub and lush Rhodes 9ths just float underneath.

styles.name: Reggae
styles.blurb: Roots reggae one-drop: dubby air, a staccato offbeat organ skank, and a deep bass that leaves the one open and lands the pocket.

styles.name: G-Funk
styles.blurb: West-coast G-funk: a whiny high synth lead sliding over a two-chord minor-9 vamp, rubber Moog bass, lazy swung hats, and clav skank on the upbeats.

styles.name: Grime
styles.blurb: Eski grime at 140: an icy square-wave riff that doubles as the bass, cold string-slam stabs, and a broken 2-step kick under sparse straight hats.

styles.name: Lo-Fi
styles.blurb: Lo-fi hip-hop: a dusty swung nod, hazy rootless Rhodes 9th loops, a lazy upright two-feel bass, and a soft flute hook that leaves most of the bar empty.

styles.name: Techno
styles.blurb: Detroit / peak-time techno: a relentless 909 four-on-the-floor, machine-straight 16th hats, a rolling synth-sub on the root, and one dark minor stab looped into hypnosis.

styles.name: Trance
styles.blurb: Uplifting trance: a four-on-the-floor 909 pulse, a rolling offbeat-16th synth bass on the root, supersaw pads pumping against the kick, and a soaring minor-key saw lead.

styles.name: Rock
styles.blurb: Classic riff rock: a straight-8 downstroke power-chord wall, a driving pick-bass root lock, and blue-note pentatonic riffs with room to ring.

styles.name: Pop
styles.blurb: Chart pop: a straight-8 piano pulse with add9 sheen, offbeat synth stabs, and an octave-pumping bass under four-on-the-floor claps.

styles.name: Punk
styles.blurb: Three-chord punk: a downstroke power-chord wall on straight 8ths, a flat-out kick-and-snare drive with zero ghost notes, and a root-locked pick bass.

styles.name: Metal
styles.blurb: Riff metal: downpicked power-chord chugs and gallops on a hard grid, a pick bass locked in unison with the kick, and dark aeolian leads over a static low root.

styles.name: Folk
styles.blurb: Front-porch folk: boom-chick steel-string guitar, an alternating root-five upright bass, and a modal fiddle air over a brushed stomp-and-tambourine pulse.
